title: X++ operators: the equal-precedence &&/|| trap, DIV/MOD, like, is/as downcast, no string interpolation
instruction: In the sandbox model, create a class DemoAccessRules whose methods each turn one X++ operator rule into code. Ground it first with get_knowledge(topic="operators-precedence"). All methods public static. (1) `boolean canPost(boolean _isAdmin, boolean _isOwner, boolean _isEnabled)` - returns true for an admin, or for an enabled owner. In X++ `&&` and `||` have EQUAL precedence and evaluate left to right, so the C#-shaped expression `_isAdmin || _isOwner && _isEnabled` silently means `(_isAdmin || _isOwner) && _isEnabled` and denies a plain admin. The returned expression MUST carry explicit parentheses around the `&&` pair, and the doc comment must state the trap. An unparenthesized mixed chain FAILS this case even though it compiles - that is the whole point of the method. (2) `int pagesFor(int _rows, int _rowsPerPage)` - whole pages plus one for any remainder, computed with the DIV and MOD KEYWORDS. Plain `/` always divides as real in X++ and FAILS this case. (3) `boolean matchesFilter(str _text, str _pattern)` - uses the `like` operator with its SQL-style wildcards (`*` any run, `?` one character); a manual strScan loop FAILS the case. (4) `str describeBuffer(Common _record)` - tests the runtime type with `is` for CustTable, downcasts with `as`, and checks the result for null BEFORE reading a field, because `as` yields null on failure rather than throwing. Confirm the buffer members you read with get_object_info before writing them. (5) `str summarise(str _left, str _right)` - joins the two with strFmt and a label. X++ has NO string interpolation: writing `$"..."` does not compile and FAILS this case. Also increment a counter somewhere with `++` as its own STATEMENT - it has no value and cannot sit inside a larger expression. The class must build with zero errors and zero BP errors.
